payload.summary: The repo is a single-notebook official codebase for the paper "Tabular Deep Learning vs Classical ML for Urban Land Cover Classification". The notebook "Urban Land Cover Classification.ipynb" has a "Random Forest" section. It trains a scikit-learn RandomForestClassifier on z-scored UCI training data, predicts on the UCI test file, and prints "Test Accuracy" with accuracy_score. This matches the claimed method, dataset, split and metric. The data files are not in the repo.

entrypoints.why: The only code file. It loads urbantraining.csv and urbantesting.csv, makes a 90/10 train/validation split of the training data, and z-scores the features. The Random Forest cell uses n_estimators=30, max_depth=5, min_samples_split=5, min_samples_leaf=3, max_features='log2', random_state=42. It fits on X_train_scaled and predicts on X_test_scaled, then prints Test Accuracy, macro P/R/F1 and AUC.

dataFiles.why: The notebook reads it from the working directory. It is presumably the UCI training.csv, renamed. The README says to put raw files in data/raw/, but the notebook uses bare relative paths.

This is the test set, presumably the UCI testing.csv, renamed. It is read as df2 and used as X_test/y_test. Get it from https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/295/urban+land+cover. The label column is 'class'.

metricSources.description: In the Random Forest code cell (after the markdown header '# Random Forest'), `test_accuracy = accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred)` is printed as `Test Accuracy: {…:.4f}`. The Logistic Regression cell and later cells use the same pattern.

payload.runInstructions:
1. Create a Python 3.10+ environment and run `pip install -r requirements.txt`. Also install scipy (used for zscore) and xlrd (imported in the first cell), because requirements.txt omits both.
2. Download the UCI Urban Land Cover dataset and put its training and testing CSVs next to the notebook, named urbantraining.csv and urbantesting.csv. The UCI originals are training.csv and testing.csv.
3. Run the notebook top to bottom, at least through the imports, data loading, validation split, normalization, the Logistic Regression cell and the Random Forest cell. The Random Forest cell reuses `class_labels` and `y_test_binarized`, which are defined only in the Logistic Regression cell, so that cell must run first.
4. Read "Test Accuracy" from the Random Forest cell output. To run headless, use `jupyter nbconvert --to notebook --execute`.
warnings: The data CSVs are not in the repo, and the notebook's filenames (urbantraining.csv, urbantesting.csv) differ from the UCI names (training.csv, testing.csv). Renaming or editing the paths is required.

The train/validation split uses random_state=None, so the training subset (90% of the training data) changes every run. The Random Forest accuracy will vary slightly between runs even though the forest has random_state=42.

Features are z-scored separately for train, validation and test, so the test set is normalised with its own statistics rather than the training statistics. The cell is as written, so keep it for fidelity.
The Random Forest cell depends on `class_labels` and `y_test_binarized` from the Logistic Regression cell and fails with a NameError if run alone.

requirements.txt lists numpy, pandas, matplotlib, scikit-learn, seaborn and jupyter, with no versions. It omits scipy and xlrd, which the notebook imports. Logistic Regression uses the `multi_class='ovr'` argument, which newer scikit-learn versions deprecate or remove, so an older version may be needed.
The README paths (notebooks/ directory, outputs/metrics.csv) do not match the repo layout. The notebook sits at the root and no metrics.csv is produced by the code I read.
I read only the first ~12 KB of the notebook, which covers the Random Forest cell. I did not review the later deep learning cells, and the saved outputs were stripped.

payload.summary: Measures the Random Forest test accuracy on the UCI testing.csv with the reviewed adapter urban-land-cover-rf-runner. The adapter re-implements the pinned notebook's Random Forest cell, because the notebook can't run as a script. I read the notebook's Random Forest cell: n_estimators=30, max_depth=5, min_samples_split=5, min_samples_leaf=3, max_features='log2', bootstrap=True, random_state=42. It fits on X_train_scaled and reports accuracy_score on the test set. The adapter matches that cell. The only deliberate change is a fixed validation-split seed of 42. The command runs the adapter on the extracted UCI training.csv and testing.csv. It writes artifacts/result.json, and metrics.accuracyPercent is read from that file. The pinned versions have binary wheels for linux/arm64 on Python 3.12. The adapter does not use matplotlib, seaborn or jupyter, so those are left out of the requirements.

The dataset extraction directory (../dataset/urban+land+cover/) and the output location (../artifacts/result.json, resolved from work/repo) are my assumptions about the lab layout. I found no dataset receipt on the board to confirm them. Adjust the paths if the lab places the files elsewhere.
In the notebook the validation split is made but never used for the Random Forest fit. The fit uses only the 90% training portion.
